classification.recommended_terminology: torsion--collision criterion in the circle group
nearest_prior_work: Kronecker's 1884 approximation theorem is the classical higher-dimensional framework for integral multiples modulo one.
Weyl's 1916 theorem places the consecutive irrational rotation orbit n alpha in the stronger uniform-distribution setting.
The exact equivalence itself is more elementary than either theorem: Q/Z is the torsion subgroup of R/Z, and an infinite sequence in a finite cyclic subgroup must collide.
classification.attribution: Present the core as elementary circle-group torsion plus pigeonhole, not as an application of Kronecker or Weyl. Cite those sources only for the classical rotation context. Credit the local work for producing the exact all-scale lattice representation of the three-prime tail and exposing collision as its universal rationality consumer.
classification.mathematical_interest: Modest as an abstract theorem, but high as a proof-interface correction: it replaces denominator-one integral-state searches by one all-denominator orbit-separation target and proves exactly what finite scans can and cannot certify.
classification.reusable_scope: Any real target admitting infinitely many integer-affine representations with pairwise-distinct integer coefficients. The offsets may vary arbitrarily because they vanish in R/Z; distinct coefficients are essential for the reverse implication.
classification.why_it_matters: For Erdős #269, rationality would force a collision somewhere in the genuine normalized tail orbit. Therefore a proof of all-scale pairwise incongruence would settle every denominator simultaneously, whereas any finite collision-free scan merely raises the minimum possible denominator.

primary_sources.author: Hermann Weyl
primary_sources.exact_anchor: The paper introduces uniform distribution modulo one and proves, in particular, uniform distribution for the consecutive multiples n alpha when alpha is irrational.
primary_sources.supports: The standard terminology of irrational circle rotations and a much stronger conclusion for consecutive sampling.
primary_sources.does_not_support: Uniform distribution along an arbitrary distinct integer sequence b_i, which can fail without additional hypotheses; no such distribution statement is used or claimed by the collision criterion.

mechanism_comparison.circle_group_torsion: The class of alpha in R/Z is torsion exactly when alpha is rational. A collision gives a nonzero integer annihilator (b_j-b_i)[alpha]=0.
mechanism_comparison.finite_orbit_pigeonhole: If alpha=p/q in lowest terms, every sampled residue lies in the q-element subgroup generated by 1/q. Infinitely many samples must collide; N distinct samples imply q>=N.
mechanism_comparison.integer_offsets: Each a_i is integral, so b_i alpha-a_i and b_i alpha define the same class modulo one. The offsets are important in the source recurrence but irrelevant to the abstract collision theorem.
mechanism_comparison.Kronecker_and_Weyl: These provide the surrounding approximation/equidistribution theory. Invoking them as the proof mechanism would inflate a one-line torsion argument and could falsely suggest distribution along arbitrary sampling times.
mechanism_comparison.local_delta: Lean proves the three-prime value's rationality creates a common all-scale lattice and then a normalized-tail collision. The card adds the reverse abstract implication, quantitative finite screens, and a sharp rational family defeating every fixed horizon.
